script: build_outputs.py (pure standard-library Python: csv/json/math/statistics/datetime/sqlite3; pandas/numpy/statsmodels unavailable in this runtime)

method.S1_geolocation_centroids: streaming pass over 1,000,163 geolocation rows -> 19,015 zip-prefix centroids (mean lat/lng), zero-padded 5-char prefixes; raw points never joined to facts
method.S2_category_filter: product_category_name_translation.csv read with utf-8-sig (header BOM stripped) -> Portuguese names telefonia / informatica_acessorios / eletronicos / consoles_games for the 4 target English categories
method.S3_fact_join: order_items -> products(category filter) -> orders (order_status='delivered' AND delivered_customer_date & estimated_delivery_date non-null) -> customers (customer_state/zip) -> sellers (seller_state/zip) -> deduped reviews (latest review_answer_timestamp) -> zip centroids; purchase_month = order_purchase_timestamp[:7]; delivery_delay_days = whole-day difference delivered - estimated (negative = early)
method.aggregation_rules: grain (seller_state, customer_state, purchase_month). Order-level metrics (avg_delivery_delay_days, avg_review_score) are de-duplicated by order_id so an order counts once per pair; item-level metrics (avg_freight_value, avg_haversine_distance_km) average over order-item rows; total_orders = distinct order_id per group (sums to 14197 because 54 orders span >1 seller-state pair, vs 14143 distinct orders overall).
method.state_pair_stats: re-aggregation of the same records: delay/review averaged over order occurrences, total_orders = sum of the pair's monthly distinct order counts, distance averaged over order-item rows with both centroids
method.overall_kpis: mean delay / review over all in-scope order occurrences (14197 / 14114), total_orders_overall = distinct order_id (14143), haversine mean over the 15,745 order items with both centroids; all rounded to 4 decimals in output.json
method.S6_series: per (seller_state, customer_state) the chronological monthly delay series; 121 of 243 pairs have >= 6 monthly points and were modelled
method.S7_arima: ARIMA(1,1,1) with constant on the differenced series: w_t = y_t-y_{t-1}, w_t = c + phi*w_{t-1} + theta*e_{t-1} + e_t, e_0=0. CSS/LS estimation: coarse grid (phi, theta step 0.1 in [-0.95,0.95]) + coordinate-wise local refinement (0.02/0.005/0.001); because the residual is linear in c, the LS constant is solved analytically from the exact quadratic SSE(c) (3 evaluations) and clipped so the asymptotic monthly drift |c/(1-phi)| cannot exceed the largest observed monthly change. 12-step forecast: w_hat_1 = c+phi*w_T+theta*e_T, w_hat_h = c+phi*w_hat_{h-1}, y_hat_h = y_T + cumsum(w_hat). forecast_mean = mean of the 12 forecast values, forecast_std = population std of the 12 values.
method.S7_fallback: fallback to historical mean / population std of the series when: <6 points, constant differenced series (max|w|=0), non-finite parameters or residuals, residual variance > variance of the differenced series, or the 12-step path leaves the historical envelope min(y)-2sd .. max(y)+2sd. 95 pairs used the ARIMA fit, 26 fell back to historical mean/std.

key_intermediate_results.overall_delay_note: average delay is negative everywhere on aggregate (~-11.77 days): orders mostly arrive before the promised date

validation.cross_check_against_pre_existing_artifac: spatiotemporal_summary (all 1844 rows), state_pair_stats (all 243 rows) and the 6 output.json KPIs reproduce the values of the pre-existing output.db/output.json in the workspace bit-for-bit (float tolerance 1e-6); the ARIMA table reproduces the same 121 state pairs, but per-pair forecast values differ from the pre-existing table because that table was produced by a different ARIMA estimation routine (its fits were heavily damped / near-flat, and the estimation code is not available). ARIMA columns are therefore reported as our own documented CSS(1,1,1) estimates.

notes_and_limitations: The 3-way grain is very sparse: 760 of 1844 monthly groups contain a single order, so monthly averages are noisy and several short series are dominated by one-off outliers.
avg_review_score is NULL for 4 groups and avg_haversine_distance_km for 9 groups (zip prefixes without geolocation); these were kept as NULL rather than imputed, as required.
Delay is a whole-day calendar difference (delivered date - estimated date), negative meaning early delivery.
Distance is symmetric in the metric but not in the grain: it is attributed to (seller_state, customer_state) pairs, so SP->RJ and RJ->SP are distinct rows.
